name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Sunday 16 September 1990

clue.text: Most of the statues are left standing

indicators.note: most of a word means nearly all its letters stay while one goes

blocks.note: taken as written before a letter is dropped

explanation.surface: After some upheaval, most of a town's statues remain upright on their plinths.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the E from the middle of STATUES to leave STATUS; 'standing' is the definition, not part of the picture of statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Status and standing are synonyms for a person's rank or position in society.

clue.text: Bert and I meet the family

indicators.note: when people meet they mingle, so the letters mingle into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone introducing their friend Bert to the relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe can mean a large family or clan group linked by common descent.

clue.text: It takes a good artist to manufacture a jewelled item

indicators.note: manufacturing makes something new out of raw material, here rearranged letters

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is crosswordese for a distinguished artist

explanation.surface: Only a skilled craftsman can make an ornament set with gems.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band or coronet worn on the head.

clue.text: Church goers stand tall!

blocks.note: setter's reading: the parts of a church that go up high and stand above the town

explanation.walkthrough: 'Church goers' suggests the congregation; read it as the parts of the church that go skywards and stand tall.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeples are the tall towers topped with spires that rise from church roofs.

clue.text: I'm to find a way to leave it out

indicators.note: finding a way implies working out a new route, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to work out how to skip a task.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to exclude or skip it, leaving it out entirely.

clue.text: Enjoy putting it on your meals

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: take great pleasure in
second meaning: a tangy condiment spread on food

explanation.surface: Advice to savour a sauce added to your dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half describes the thing rather than naming it: a condiment is what you put on meals.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means savour with pleasure; as a noun it is a pickle or chutney served with food.

clue.text: It will lower his reputation if Ed gets mean

indicators.note: a weak signal: a person who gets mean changes character, so the letters change order

blocks.note: the word itself is also fodder

explanation.surface: Ed will be thought less of if he turns stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' does double duty: it is part of the letters as well as the change in Ed's character.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to degrade them or cause a loss of dignity and respect.

clue.text: Peter went mad when they interfered with it

indicators.note: to go mad here is to lose order, so the letters beside it are scrambled

explanation.surface: Peter lost his temper when people meddled with his things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went mad' reads as Peter's anger, but 'went' is the signal and 'mad' joins Peter as letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamper with something is to meddle or interfere with it, usually in an unwelcome way.

clue.text: It's just an illusion that I'm changing gear

indicators.note: changing the order of letters produces a new word from the same set

explanation.surface: A driver insists the sense of shifting gears is only in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as the shimmer of water seen on a hot road.

clue.text: That is how dental work may be brought on inevitably

indicators.note: to work material is to shape it into a new form, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Seems to explain how a trip to the dentist becomes unavoidable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dental work' reads as one idea, but 'work' is the signal acting on 'dental' plus the abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: When one thing entails another, it involves it as a necessary consequence.

clue.text: Camped out only to make off secretly

indicators.note: out can mean out of order or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Campers spent a night outdoors only to slip away before dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, often to avoid paying or being caught.

clue.text: I con them out of their money

indicators.note: out suggests out of order, so the short phrase is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the space dropped

explanation.surface: A swindler confesses to cheating people of their cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Coin is metal currency, and as a mass noun it stands for money in general.

clue.text: Walking strangely after having had lunch on the rig

indicators.note: something done strangely is done in an odd way, so the letters come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: An oil-rig worker staggers about after a heavy lunch on the platform.
explanation.walkthrough: A rig is an offshore oil platform. 'Walking strangely' reads as one phrase, but 'strangely' is the signal; the definition 'Walking' is a loose one for an unsteady gait.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurching is moving with sudden unsteady lurches, a stumbling kind of walking.

clue.text: He saves us from a mere deer?

indicators.note: a weak signal: something made from other material is rebuilt out of it

explanation.surface: A whimsical question whether a mere deer could be a saviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the absurd picture of a deer as rescuer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Redeemer is a Christian title for Christ, the one who saves humankind from sin.

clue.text: Lo! I'd go all out to be worshipped

definitions.note: describes a noun: something to be worshipped

indicators.note: going all out suggests letters thrown out of their places and reset

explanation.surface: A devotee declares they would make every effort to be revered.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or person venerated as a god, an object of worship.

clue.text: Thrown into disorder while having fun with codes

indicators.note: putting something into disorder jumbles it, so the letters that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone playing about with ciphers gets everything in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown into disorder' looks like the whole definition, but 'Thrown' alone defines and 'into disorder' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thrown by something is to be disconcerted or bewildered by it.

clue.text: Alternatively, a hill will do for such a good speaker

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A speaker might use either a podium or a hilltop to address a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is an eloquent public speaker, someone skilled in making speeches.

clue.text: A noisy quarrel in a car isn't all that safe

blocks.note: the plain meaning: a loud row

blocks.clueFragment: in a car isn't all that safe
blocks.note: a comment that a row while driving is dangerous, with no clear letter play

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plain; the rest seems only to add colour, as no tidy letter play from it builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy disturbance or brawl, a loud quarrel involving several people.

clue.text: Most beagles keep birds

indicators.note: most of a word is all but one of its letters, here losing its opening

blocks.note: taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A claim that most hunting dogs are kept for guarding poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagles are large birds of prey, so they are an example of birds.

clue.text: Pastimes known for a thousand ages

indicators.note: a weak signal: the letters are taken for something other than they seem

blocks.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Some amusements have been played for countless centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Games are activities played for amusement, so they are pastimes.

clue.text: Lee's a one that needs your support

explanation.surface: Lee is someone who always leans on others.
explanation.walkthrough: No clear signal word appears; the letters of "Lee's a" simply rearrange, and the definition is a teasing description.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds a painting, so it is the thing providing support rather than needing it.

clue.text: Apt to raise it for some hangers-on

definitions.note: plural definition for a singular answer

indicators.note: a loose signal: the letters are rearranged to serve some other purpose

explanation.surface: Suggests some freeloaders are likely to bring a subject up.
explanation.walkthrough: The signal is vague; the letters of 'Apt' and 'raise' rearrange exactly, and the plural 'hangers-on' loosely defines a singular word.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite is a person who lives off others without giving anything back, a sponger or hanger-on.

clue.text: It is repeated for a goddess

explanation.surface: A remark that a word is said twice when addressing a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis is the ancient Egyptian goddess of motherhood and magic, wife of Osiris.

clue.text: Sam and I see the Medical Officer at the plant

indicators.note: a weak signal: the named people are to be seen together in a new arrangement

blocks.note: MO is the abbreviation for Medical Officer

explanation.surface: Two people visit the works doctor at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory where the Medical Officer works, but it is the definition: a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a shrub or tree with fluffy yellow flowers, often called wattle in Australia.

clue.text: Love moving its tail - it's so flighty!

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift position and settle in a new order

blocks.note: the word tail taken as written

explanation.surface: A lovesick bird wags its tail, being such a fickle creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone volatile is changeable and unpredictable in mood, like a fickle, flighty person.

clue.text: Make little noise when you steal cattle

blocks.note: first meaning: make a soft crackling sound, as leaves do

explanation.surface: Advice to a cattle thief to keep quiet during the raid.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both the soft swishing of dry leaves and stock theft, as in a cattle rustler.
